```plato

    //==
    // # Gradients and surface normals
    //
    // Bodies for the differentiable SDF interfaces
    // (`implicit-sdf.concepts.plato`). The gradient of an exact distance field is
    // its outward normal direction, so reporting one makes every gradient-derived
    // helper in `fields-implicits.library.plato` — `SurfaceNormalAt`,
    // `BoundaryNormalAt`, `SlopeAt`, `IsStationaryAt` — resolve against an SDF.
    //
    // None of the stored forms can be differentiated symbolically: `FunctionSdf*`
    // holds an opaque lambda and `SampledSdf*` holds a lattice, so both difference
    // the field numerically. `PlacedSdf*` is the exception — a rigid placement
    // rotates the source gradient rather than re-differencing it, which is the
    // whole reason the gradient travels through the interface instead of being
    // recomputed by each caller.

    // The finite-difference step used to estimate an SDF gradient. Far above
    // `Number.Epsilon`, where a difference quotient would be rounding noise rather
    // than signal, and well below the feature size the distance primitives are
    // written for.
    SdfGradientStep(_: Number): Number
        => 0.0001;
```
